name: Silhouette Soft

lead: Silhouette Soft is a branded, CE-marked suspension suture used in thread lifts. Absorbable threads with cones are placed under the skin to reposition tissue on the brows, midface, jawline and neck, giving a lifted look without removing skin.

A 2019 study of 193 patients using Silhouette Soft threads found high satisfaction at six months. Research is mostly small prospective studies and biomechanical modelling; larger comparative trials are limited.

paras: A clinician places the threads through fine needles or cannulas under the skin and anchors them to lift tissue. Patients in the 2019 study were followed at one week and at one, three and six months after the procedure. Common treatment areas were the jawline, midface, eyebrows and neck.

Thread lifts as a group have documented risks. A doctor quoted on Wikipedia has called the category 'the most dangerous procedure an aesthetic practitioner can do', and a BBC investigation of training courses found infection-control and technique problems. Choosing a qualified clinician is the usual safety guidance.

angle.text: Silhouette Soft is used to lift sagging tissue on the face and neck. In the 2019 study the most common sites were the jawline, midface, eyebrows and neck.

lead: Silhouette Soft is a CE-marked suspension suture system designed for repositioning soft tissues of the face and neck.[1] Absorbable threads fitted with cones are placed under the skin to lift tissue and give a firmer jawline, midface and brow.[2]

A thread lift (also called a non-surgical face lift) uses barbed or coned threads to pull facial and neck skin upward without removing skin.[3] Silhouette Soft belongs to the absorbable cone-thread type.

In a 2019 prospective study of 193 patients (mean age about 52, range 25 to 89) lifted with Silhouette Soft and a double-needle technique, patient satisfaction rose from 94% at one week to 99% at six months, and two surgeons rated outcomes similarly high.[2] Other published work covers a cadaver finite-element model of the suture and a trial of the threads in nasal valve stenosis.[4][1]

paras: Silhouette Soft is described in the literature as a CE-marked medical device for repositioning facial and neck soft tissue.[1] The threads are absorbable and self-retaining, made with polylactic acid cones.[4]
Thread lifts in general are sometimes called non-surgical face lifts because they lift tissue without skin excision.[3]

Wikipedia reports that a cosmetic doctor called thread lifts 'the most dangerous procedure an aesthetic practitioner can do', that a BBC undercover investigation of training courses found poor infection control and punctured blood vessels, and that in the UK practitioners are not required to hold mandatory qualifications.[3] That article focuses on non-absorbable threads; the Silhouette Soft threads discussed here are absorbable.

A 2019 prospective chart review in the Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology followed 193 patients (23 men, 170 women) treated with Silhouette Soft threads and the Promo Happy Lift double-needle technique between January 2016 and May 2017. Outcomes were rated with the GAIS score at one week and at one, three and six months; patient satisfaction rose from 94% to 99%, and surgeons' ratings rose from 94% to 99% and from 83% to 98%.[2]

A 2019 Facial Plastic Surgery trial of 60 patients used Silhouette Soft cone threads for a nasal valve lift in nasal valve stenosis over two years.[4] A 2023 cadaver study ran finite-element simulations of the suture's interaction with facial soft tissue.[1] A 2025 review of breast thread lifting covers a different body area but describes the same minimally invasive thread approach.[5]
